subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw core add an opt-in `models status --probe --all` mode for live checks of every configured model, and what exact CLI/JSON/error contract should it expose?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change adds a new user-facing live provider/model probe mode that can consume tokens, hit rate limits, overlap fallback diagnostics, and set expectations for JSON status consumers.

options.title: Sponsor core `--probe --all`
options.body: Settle the cost, rate-limit, timeout/concurrency, JSON, and redaction contract, then implement the focused core CLI change.

options.title: Fold into broader model diagnostics
options.body: Use this report as input to a larger fallback-chain or staged model-migration diagnostic design instead of adding a standalone flag now.

options.title: Decline new core mode
options.body: Keep `models status --probe` provider/auth-focused and document scripts or external tooling for per-model sweeps.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core `--probe --all`
recommendation.body: Settle the cost, rate-limit, timeout/concurrency, JSON, and redaction contract, then implement the focused core CLI change.

likelyOwner.reason: The current auth-probe surface was introduced by Peter Steinberger and this is a core CLI/product contract decision in that same area.
